title: Identity Landing Zone: SSO/RBAC/KMS Acceptance & Audit Readiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD fragment and acceptance checklist for the Identity Landing Zone feature required for Private and VPC customer onboarding. Covers SSO/SAML & OIDC integration patterns, SCIM provisioning, RBAC role matrix, immutable audit logging (retention and export), and KMS/HSM key custody options. Objective: define unambiguous acceptance criteria and required artifacts for Legal/Security/Eng sign-off before GA for regulated customers.
scope_clarifications: In-scope: SSO (SAML 2.0 + OIDC), SCIM user provisioning, RBAC role definitions for platform and audit roles, server-side audit log immutability and export, KMS envelope encryption integration and optional HSM-backed key provider.

Out-of-scope: full IAM federation with customer IdP user attributes mapping beyond standard claims, audit analytics UI (only log export and schema defined), and cross-account key escrow workflows (future work).
Optional path: provide a managed KMS tenant for smaller customers vs. customer-managed HSM for enterprise (decision to be gated by legal and procurement).

Migration: existing hosted customers wanting Private should be supported with an opt-in key rotation and audit continuity plan; this ticket defines acceptance evidence but not migration tooling implementation details.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Platform accepts both SAML 2.0 IdP metadata upload and OIDC discovery URL; successful authentication test with at least two major IdPs (Azure AD and Okta) recorded in CI e2e checks.
SCIM: SCIM v2 provisioning endpoints implement user create/update/deactivate and return standardized 200/409/400 responses; documented schema mapping in Confluence.

RBAC: Role matrix defined with least-privilege defaults; roles include: org-admin, billing-admin, deployment-operator, read-only-audit; each role has explicit allowed API scopes and UI capabilities documented.

Audit logs: All admin and auth events (login, token issuance, role changes, KMS operations) are written to append-only logs with immutable object storage and tamper-evidence (signed entries). Retention policy configurable by tenant (default 90 days) and exportable in NDJSON with timestamped manifests.

KMS/HSM: KMS integration supports both customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault and an HSM-backed option that meets FIPS 140-2 level 3 requirements. End-to-end key usage flows (encryption, rotation, revoke) have automated test coverage and a documented recovery playbook.

Compliance artifacts: Deliverable evidence includes Confluence PRD, test-run artifacts (CI logs), a signed checklist from Security, Legal, and Product, and a demo replay video showing IdP SSO+SCIM provisioning and an audit log export.
decisions: Prefer OIDC as primary recommendation for new integrations due to modern OAuth flows; SAML retained for enterprise IdPs that require it.
Provide two telemetry tiers: minimal audit metadata for latency-sensitive paths and full verbose audit for regulated customers. Default is minimal to limit cost, configurable per-tenant.
Choose signed append-only log objects over proprietary ledger for initial release to simplify ops while preserving tamper evidence.
HSM option will be offered as a professional-services-backed setup for GA; managed HSM automation slated for a follow-up engineering epic.
risks: Delaying HSM automation increases manual setup effort for early enterprise customers and may slow sales cycles in highly regulated verticals.
Misalignment between RBAC semantics across Console and API could cause privilege gaps; require parallel API and UI RBAC integration tests.
Audit log size and storage costs may grow nonlinearly for high-volume tenants; need quotas and retention guardrails to avoid runaway costs.
Key rotation and recovery flows must be validated to avoid data inaccessibility; emergency key-unwrap procedures require operator playbooks and customer sign-off.
dependencies: PM-71234 (evidence package and operational signoff for private keying)
checklist: Confluence PRD reviewed by Security and Legal (link in links).
E2E test: successful SSO+SCIM run against Okta and Azure AD recorded in CI artifacts.
RBAC matrix approved by Product, Security, and a Solutions Engineer with at least one customer mapping example.
Audit log retention UI + export tested; NDJSON export validated against schema by QA.
KMS/HSM integration validated with key creation, usage, rotation, revoke; HSM validation includes FIPS certificate review.
